quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Coach Ibrahim's team lost their first four games of the season by wide margins. In their fifth game, after switching to a completely different defensive strategy, they held their opponents to their lowest score of the year and won by ten points.
options: The team lost the fifth game as well.
The team's defensive strategy stayed exactly the same all season.
The new defensive strategy appears to have helped the team perform better.
The opponent's score had no connection to the team's strategy.
quests.correctAnswer: The new defensive strategy appears to have helped the team perform better.
quests.hint: Compare how the team performed before and after changing strategy.
quests.explanation: The team's performance improved sharply right after switching defensive strategies, suggesting the new approach made a real difference.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Two competing phone companies released nearly identical models this year, but one company priced its phone $200 lower. Within weeks, tech reviewers noted that the cheaper phone was outselling its rival by a wide margin in every region they tracked.
options: The more expensive phone outsold the cheaper one everywhere.
Both phones sold in exactly equal numbers.
The two phones were priced exactly the same.
Price seems to have been the main reason shoppers preferred one phone.
quests.correctAnswer: Price seems to have been the main reason shoppers preferred one phone.
quests.hint: Think about the one major difference reviewers noticed between the two phones.
quests.explanation: With nearly identical phones but a $200 price gap, the cheaper one sold far better, suggesting price was the deciding factor for most buyers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Every time his younger sister calls with a problem, David drops whatever he's doing to help, even if it means leaving work early or cancelling his own plans.
options: David is a very devoted older brother.
David rarely has time for his sister.
David refuses to help his sister with problems.
David and his sister never speak to each other.
quests.correctAnswer: David is a very devoted older brother.
quests.hint: Think about what David's actions reveal about how he feels toward his sister.
quests.explanation: Dropping everything to help his sister, even at a cost to himself, shows how devoted David is to her.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: The marketing department used to submit expense reports on paper, a process that took an average of two weeks to get approved. After moving the process online, most reports are now approved within two business days, according to the finance team.
options: The online system has sped up expense report approval significantly.
The online system made approvals take longer than before.
The finance team stopped approving expense reports.
How reports are submitted has no bearing on approval speed.
quests.correctAnswer: The online system has sped up expense report approval significantly.
quests.hint: Compare how long approval took before and after the process moved online.
quests.explanation: Approval time dropped from two weeks to about two days after the switch to an online system, showing the new process is much faster.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Scientists studying a local river noticed that fish populations had been declining for a decade. After a nearby factory installed new water treatment equipment two years ago, researchers have recorded a steady increase in several fish species.
options: Fish populations continued declining after the equipment was installed.
The new water treatment equipment may have improved conditions for the fish.
The factory removed all of its water treatment equipment.
Water treatment equipment has no relationship to fish populations.
quests.correctAnswer: The new water treatment equipment may have improved conditions for the fish.
quests.hint: Compare the trend in fish populations before and after the treatment equipment was installed.
quests.explanation: Fish populations began recovering only after the new treatment equipment was installed, suggesting cleaner water conditions supported the fish.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: One clothing brand keeps its prices fixed all year, while a competing brand runs frequent seasonal sales. Market researchers found that customers of the second brand tend to delay purchases, often waiting for the next sale before buying anything at full price.
options: Frequent sales encourage customers to buy immediately at full price.
Customers of the second brand never wait for sales.
The first brand also runs frequent seasonal sales.
Frequent sales may be training customers to avoid paying full price.
quests.correctAnswer: Frequent sales may be training customers to avoid paying full price.
quests.hint: Think about what habit customers might develop if discounts happen often.
quests.explanation: Customers of the brand with frequent sales tend to wait for discounts, suggesting the frequent sales have trained them to delay full-price purchases.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university professor noticed that students who attended her optional weekly review sessions scored, on average, twelve points higher on the final exam than students who never attended, even though attendance had no effect on their grade.
options: Students who attended review sessions scored lower on average.
Attendance at review sessions directly determined students' grades.
Attending the review sessions appears linked to stronger exam performance.
There was no difference in scores between the two groups.
quests.correctAnswer: Attending the review sessions appears linked to stronger exam performance.
quests.hint: Compare the average exam scores of students who attended sessions with those who didn't.
quests.explanation: Students who attended the optional sessions scored noticeably higher on average, suggesting a connection between attending and performing well, even though attendance wasn't required or graded.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A workplace wellness survey found that employees who took a ten-minute break every two hours reported significantly lower afternoon fatigue than employees who worked straight through without stopping.
options: Employees who took breaks reported more fatigue than those who didn't.
Taking breaks had no connection to how tired employees felt.
All employees in the survey reported the same fatigue levels.
Regular short breaks seem to reduce afternoon fatigue at work.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular short breaks seem to reduce afternoon fatigue at work.
quests.hint: Compare fatigue levels between employees who took breaks and those who didn't.
quests.explanation: Employees who took regular breaks reported less fatigue than those who worked without stopping, suggesting the breaks helped reduce tiredness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Whenever a new neighbor moves onto the street, Mrs. Ferreira is the first to knock on their door with a plate of homemade cookies and a list of nearby stores and restaurants.
options: Mrs. Ferreira avoids speaking to new neighbors.
Mrs. Ferreira has never met any of her neighbors.
Mrs. Ferreira dislikes when new people move onto the street.
Mrs. Ferreira likes to make new neighbors feel welcome.
quests.correctAnswer: Mrs. Ferreira likes to make new neighbors feel welcome.
quests.hint: Think about what Mrs. Ferreira's actions suggest about her attitude toward new neighbors.
quests.explanation: Greeting every new neighbor with cookies and helpful information shows that Mrs. Ferreira makes an effort to welcome people to the street.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Airlines that offer free seat selection at booking tend to receive fewer complaints about families being seated apart than airlines that charge an extra fee for choosing seats in advance.
options: Charging for seat selection may be linked to more separated-family complaints.
Free seat selection leads to more complaints about family seating.
Seat selection policies have no connection to family seating complaints.
All airlines charge the same fee for seat selection.
quests.correctAnswer: Charging for seat selection may be linked to more separated-family complaints.
quests.hint: Compare the complaint patterns between airlines with different seat selection policies.
quests.explanation: Airlines that charge for seat selection see more complaints about separated families, suggesting the fee may prevent some families from choosing seats together.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A food critic ate at three restaurants owned by the same chef. The two restaurants that used locally sourced ingredients received glowing reviews, while the one that relied mainly on imported, frozen ingredients received a lukewarm response.
options: The critic preferred the restaurant using imported ingredients.
The critic seemed to prefer the meals made with local ingredients.
All three restaurants received the same review from the critic.
The critic did not mention ingredients in any of the reviews.
quests.correctAnswer: The critic seemed to prefer the meals made with local ingredients.
quests.hint: Compare how the critic responded to each type of restaurant.
quests.explanation: The restaurants using local ingredients earned glowing reviews while the one using frozen, imported ingredients did not, suggesting the critic favored the fresher, local approach.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city council member proposed closing the downtown street to cars every Sunday to create a pedestrian zone. Local business owners were divided: several restaurant owners supported the idea, while shop owners who depend on customers arriving by car spoke against it.
options: Every business owner in the meeting supported the proposal.
Business owners' opinions on the proposal varied depending on their type of business.
Every business owner in the meeting opposed the proposal.
The type of business had no relation to owners' opinions.
quests.correctAnswer: Business owners' opinions on the proposal varied depending on their type of business.
quests.hint: Notice which kinds of businesses supported the idea and which opposed it.
quests.explanation: Restaurant owners tended to support the pedestrian zone while car-dependent shop owners opposed it, showing that the type of business shaped each owner's opinion.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A tech company tested two versions of its website checkout page with different groups of shoppers. The version with fewer steps led to noticeably more completed purchases than the version with additional confirmation screens.
options: The version with more steps led to more completed purchases.
A simpler checkout process seems to lead to more completed purchases.
Both versions of the checkout page performed identically.
The number of steps in checkout has no effect on purchases.
quests.correctAnswer: A simpler checkout process seems to lead to more completed purchases.
quests.hint: Compare how the two checkout versions performed.
quests.explanation: The shorter checkout process resulted in more completed purchases than the longer one, suggesting that reducing steps helps shoppers finish buying.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A financial counselor found that clients who automatically transferred a fixed amount into savings each payday, before spending on anything else, ended the year with far larger savings balances than clients who saved only whatever was left over at month's end.
options: Saving money automatically before spending appears more effective than saving what's left over.
Saving leftover money at month's end resulted in larger savings.
Both saving methods produced identical results.
When money is saved during the month makes no difference.
quests.correctAnswer: Saving money automatically before spending appears more effective than saving what's left over.
quests.hint: Compare the savings outcomes for the two different approaches.
quests.explanation: Clients who saved automatically before spending ended up with larger savings than those who saved whatever was left, suggesting the timing of saving matters.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A streaming service noticed that shows released all at once, with every episode available immediately, were often finished by viewers within the first week. Shows released one episode per week kept viewers actively watching and discussing the series for months.
options: Shows released all at once kept audiences engaged for longer.
Release schedules have no effect on how long viewers stay engaged.
Both release methods kept viewers engaged for the same amount of time.
Weekly releases seem to keep audiences engaged with a show for longer.
quests.correctAnswer: Weekly releases seem to keep audiences engaged with a show for longer.
quests.hint: Compare how long viewer engagement lasted under each release method.
quests.explanation: Weekly releases kept viewers watching and talking about a show for months, while shows released all at once were often finished within a week, suggesting the weekly format sustains engagement longer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Whenever her grandchildren visit, Mrs. Ahmadi puts away her phone completely and spends the entire afternoon playing games or reading with them, no matter how busy her day has been.
options: Mrs. Ahmadi avoids spending time with her grandchildren.
Mrs. Ahmadi is usually busy with her phone during visits.
Mrs. Ahmadi prioritizes spending focused time with her grandchildren.
Mrs. Ahmadi's grandchildren rarely visit her.
quests.correctAnswer: Mrs. Ahmadi prioritizes spending focused time with her grandchildren.
quests.hint: Think about what putting away her phone during visits suggests about her priorities.
quests.explanation: Setting aside her phone completely to focus on her grandchildren shows that Mrs. Ahmadi makes their time together a priority.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A software company allowed one team to work entirely from home while a similar team continued coming into the office. After six months, the remote team had shipped more product updates, while the in-office team reported stronger scores on measures of team bonding.
options: Each work arrangement seemed to have its own distinct advantage.
The remote team performed better in every single measure.
The in-office team performed better in every single measure.
Working from home or the office made no measurable difference at all.
quests.correctAnswer: Each work arrangement seemed to have its own distinct advantage.
quests.hint: Notice that each team excelled in a different area, not the same one.
quests.explanation: The remote team shipped more updates while the in-office team scored higher on bonding, showing that each arrangement offered a different kind of benefit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A youth soccer league changed its rules so that every player, regardless of skill level, had to play at least half of each game. The following season, overall enrollment in the league grew by nearly a third, according to league organizers.
options: The new playing-time rule may have made the league more appealing to families.
Enrollment in the league dropped after the rule was introduced.
The league removed the new playing-time rule after one season.
How much a child plays has no bearing on whether families join a league.
quests.correctAnswer: The new playing-time rule may have made the league more appealing to families.
quests.hint: Think about what might frustrate families in a league where only the best players get to play.
quests.explanation: Enrollment grew substantially after the league guaranteed playing time for every player, suggesting the change addressed a common frustration and attracted more families.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A survey of online shoppers found that listings with at least five customer photos received far more clicks than listings with only the seller's professional photos, even when the products themselves were identical.
options: Listings with only professional photos received more clicks.
The number of photos in a listing has no effect on clicks.
Customer photos seem to make listings more appealing to shoppers.
All listings in the survey received the same number of clicks.
quests.correctAnswer: Customer photos seem to make listings more appealing to shoppers.
quests.hint: Compare how listings performed based on the type of photos they included.
quests.explanation: Listings with customer photos received far more clicks than those with only professional photos, suggesting that shoppers respond well to seeing real customer images.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A clinic tracked patients who received a text message reminder the day before their appointment and compared them to patients who received no reminder at all. The reminder group missed far fewer appointments over the following year.
options: Patients who received reminders missed more appointments.
Text reminders appear to reduce the number of missed appointments.
Text reminders had no effect on missed appointments.
Every patient in the study missed the same number of appointments.
quests.correctAnswer: Text reminders appear to reduce the number of missed appointments.
quests.hint: Compare how many appointments each group missed.
quests.explanation: Patients who received text reminders missed far fewer appointments than those who didn't, suggesting the reminders were effective at reducing no-shows.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city compared two recycling programs: one where residents sorted recyclables into separate bins, and another where all recyclables went into a single bin to be sorted later at a facility. The single-bin program saw a much higher rate of resident participation, but a higher rate of contamination from non-recyclable items.
options: The single-bin program was better in every measurable way.
Each recycling program came with its own trade-off.
The sorted-bin program was better in every measurable way.
Both programs produced identical results in every category.
quests.correctAnswer: Each recycling program came with its own trade-off.
quests.hint: Notice that the single-bin program did better on one measure but worse on another.
quests.explanation: The single-bin program increased participation but also increased contamination, showing that neither approach was simply better overall — each had a cost and a benefit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Every morning before work, Tomas checks the weather app, lays out his clothes for the next day, and packs his lunch the night before, a routine he says he has followed without fail for the past five years.
options: Tomas rarely plans ahead for his workday.
Tomas changes his morning routine frequently.
Tomas relies on a consistent daily routine to prepare for work.
Tomas stopped preparing for work five years ago.
quests.correctAnswer: Tomas relies on a consistent daily routine to prepare for work.
quests.hint: Think about what these repeated daily habits suggest about how Tomas approaches his mornings.
quests.explanation: Following the same preparation steps every day for five years shows that Tomas depends on a consistent routine to get ready for work.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A high school introduced a peer-tutoring program in which stronger students helped classmates who were struggling in the same subject. At the end of the year, both the students who received tutoring and the students who provided it showed improved grades in that subject.
options: Only the students who received tutoring showed improvement.
The peer-tutoring program appears to have benefited both groups of students.
Only the students who provided tutoring showed improvement.
Neither group of students showed any improvement.
quests.correctAnswer: The peer-tutoring program appears to have benefited both groups of students.
quests.hint: Notice that the passage mentions improvement for two different groups, not just one.
quests.explanation: Both the tutors and the students they helped showed improved grades, suggesting the program benefited everyone involved, not just the students receiving help.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A travel booking site found that customers who could see real-time seat maps before choosing a flight were less likely to cancel their bookings afterward than customers who booked without seeing a seat map at all.
options: Seeing a seat map in advance may reduce the likelihood of cancellations.
Customers who saw seat maps cancelled more often.
Seat maps had no effect on cancellation rates.
Every customer in the study cancelled their booking.
quests.correctAnswer: Seeing a seat map in advance may reduce the likelihood of cancellations.
quests.hint: Compare cancellation rates between customers who saw seat maps and those who didn't.
quests.explanation: Customers who could view seat maps before booking cancelled less often, suggesting that having this information upfront helped them feel more confident in their choice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A museum exhibit featuring interactive touchscreens next to each painting kept visitors in that gallery for an average of twenty-five minutes, compared to just under eight minutes in a nearby gallery with traditional printed placards only.
options: Visitors spent less time in the gallery with touchscreens.
Both galleries kept visitors for the same amount of time.
The interactive touchscreens seem to have kept visitors engaged longer.
The type of display information has no effect on how long visitors stay.
quests.correctAnswer: The interactive touchscreens seem to have kept visitors engaged longer.
quests.hint: Compare how long visitors stayed in each gallery.
quests.explanation: Visitors spent more than three times as long in the gallery with interactive touchscreens, suggesting the interactive format held their attention longer than printed placards.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city installed benches and shade structures along a previously bare stretch of sidewalk near a senior center. Within a few months, staff at the center noticed far more elderly residents walking that route instead of driving short distances.
options: The new benches and shade may have encouraged more walking among seniors.
Fewer seniors walked that route after the benches were installed.
The city removed the benches shortly after installing them.
Benches and shade have no connection to how people choose to travel.
quests.correctAnswer: The new benches and shade may have encouraged more walking among seniors.
quests.hint: Think about what might make a walking route more appealing to older adults.
quests.explanation: More seniors began walking the route after benches and shade were added, suggesting the improvements made walking a more comfortable option.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A meal-kit company found that customers who received recipes rated 'easy' by other subscribers renewed their subscriptions at a higher rate than customers who mostly received recipes rated 'difficult,' even when the ingredients cost about the same.
options: Recipe difficulty had no connection to subscription renewals.
Customers receiving difficult recipes renewed more often.
Recipe difficulty appears to influence whether customers keep their subscriptions.
Ingredient cost was the main factor in subscription renewals.
quests.correctAnswer: Recipe difficulty appears to influence whether customers keep their subscriptions.
quests.hint: Compare renewal rates between customers receiving easy versus difficult recipes.
quests.explanation: Customers who received easier recipes renewed their subscriptions more often than those who mostly got difficult ones, suggesting recipe difficulty plays a role in customer satisfaction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A retirement plan administrator found that employees automatically enrolled in the company's savings plan, with the option to opt out, ended up saving at much higher rates than employees who had to actively sign up to join the same plan.
options: Requiring active sign-up led to higher savings rates.
Automatic enrollment appears more effective at increasing participation than requiring sign-up.
Both enrollment methods produced identical savings rates.
How employees enroll in a savings plan makes no difference to participation.
quests.correctAnswer: Automatic enrollment appears more effective at increasing participation than requiring sign-up.
quests.hint: Compare savings rates between the two enrollment methods.
quests.explanation: Employees who were automatically enrolled saved at higher rates than those who had to sign up themselves, suggesting the default option made a real difference in participation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A cybersecurity firm compared companies that required employees to change passwords every thirty days with companies that instead required longer, more complex passwords changed only once a year. The second group reported fewer security breaches overall.
options: Frequent password changes led to fewer security breaches.
Password policy had no connection to the number of breaches.
Both groups reported the exact same number of breaches.
Longer, less frequently changed passwords may be more effective at preventing breaches.
quests.correctAnswer: Longer, less frequently changed passwords may be more effective at preventing breaches.
quests.hint: Compare breach rates between the two password policies.
quests.explanation: Companies using longer passwords changed less often had fewer breaches than those requiring frequent changes, suggesting password complexity may matter more than how often passwords change.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A youth swim coach began ending every practice with five minutes of stretching and light conversation, rather than dismissing swimmers as soon as their laps were finished. Over the following season, fewer swimmers dropped out of the program compared to previous years.
options: More swimmers dropped out after the new routine began.
The coach removed the stretching routine after one season.
How practice ends has no bearing on whether swimmers stay in the program.
Ending practice with a relaxed wind-down may have improved swimmer retention.
quests.correctAnswer: Ending practice with a relaxed wind-down may have improved swimmer retention.
quests.hint: Compare how many swimmers stayed in the program before and after the new routine began.
quests.explanation: Fewer swimmers quit the program after practices began ending with a relaxed cooldown, suggesting the change helped swimmers feel more positive about staying.
